{{Expand section|date=July 2014}}

The '''principle of nonvacuous contrast''' is a logical or methodological principle which requires that a genuine [[Predicate (grammar)|predicate]] never refer to everything, or to nothing, within its [[universe of discourse]]. The implications of this is that for a predicate to be meaningful it can neither apply to all members of a group or to no members of the group.
